title: How to Choose a Water Bottle: Size, Lid and Material
h1: How to Choose a Water Bottle
metaDescription: Steel or plastic, straw or chug lid, 24 or 40 ounces? How to choose a water bottle you'll actually use.
lede: A great water bottle fits your day. Pick the size and lid first, then the brand.

p: Bigger means fewer refills but more weight. As a rough guide:
list: 18 to 24 oz: bags, kids and short trips
26 to 32 oz: all-day desk or gym use
40 oz and up: long drives and people who drink a lot, usually as tumblers with handles

p: The lid decides how you drink and whether it leaks:
list: Straw lids: easy sipping, but usually not leakproof when tipped
Chug or spout lids: fast drinking, often leak-resistant
Screw caps: the most leakproof, but slower to drink from

p: Double-wall vacuum-insulated steel keeps drinks cold for hours and doesn't sweat on the outside, but is heavier. Plastic bottles are lighter and cheaper but don't insulate.
Wide bottles often don't fit car cup holders. A wide mouth makes adding ice and cleaning much easier, and simpler lids have fewer parts to scrub.

faqs.q: How do I clean a water bottle?
faqs.a: Wash it regularly with warm soapy water and a bottle brush, and take the lid apart if it's designed to come apart. Let everything dry fully before reassembling.
Usually from residue in the lid or straw. Clean all lid parts separately and let them dry completely.
